purpose: Curated, first-party DreamCo learning overlays for public freeCodeCamp video metadata. Overrides survive catalog refreshes and define education routing, original practice, capability/tool/agent links, and reproducible Buddy demonstrations.
truth_boundary: A catalog row is not a studied lesson, transcript, permission grant, model-training dataset, or mastery result.
These are original DreamCo implementation briefs based on public course descriptions and chapter outlines; do not reproduce third-party course transcripts or protected course materials.
Division targets route learning resources only. They do not grant runtime permissions, financial authority, or production access.
Model weight training requires separately verified source rights, approved datasets, reproducible runs, checkpoint hashes, and holdout/regression evidence.

entries.title: Python Algorithmic Trading with SnapTrade, Massive, Alpaca
entries.objective: Build a reproducible, risk-controlled momentum research and paper-trading system. The course describes a 12-month lookback that excludes the most recent month, a Django application, Massive market data, SnapTrade brokerage connectivity, and Alpaca execution.
implementation_steps: Define the strategy hypothesis, asset universe, benchmark, evaluation period, and explicit non-goals.
Create a Django project with versioned instruments, bars, corporate actions, strategy configurations, signals, orders, fills, and audit records.
Build a Massive market-data adapter with pagination, rate limits, source timestamps, adjusted-price handling, and immutable raw snapshots.
Validate missing bars, duplicate timestamps, symbol changes, splits, dividends, survivorship bias, and look-ahead leakage.
Calculate momentum over the prior 12 months while excluding the most recent month; pin the exact formula and trading calendar.
Rank the eligible universe and generate deterministic buy/sell candidates with explainable factor inputs.
Backtest using point-in-time data, realistic transaction costs, spread, slippage, market impact assumptions, and out-of-sample periods.
Add portfolio constraints: per-position limits, concentration limits, max drawdown stop, daily loss limit, exposure caps, and a global kill switch.
Record every signal, decision, rejected order, simulated fill, and metric with reproducible strategy/data versions.
Connect SnapTrade only for approved account discovery/read-only context; keep broker credentials in the secret manager.
Route orders exclusively to Alpaca paper trading; verify order state transitions, retries, idempotency, and cancel behavior.
Run walk-forward validation, stress tests, transaction-cost sensitivity, and a paper-trading soak before any production review.
entries.practice: Buddy builds a synthetic-data momentum research lab, replays historical fixtures, compares baseline and candidate strategies, and emits a paper-trading report with risk limits and an audit trail.
entries.assessment: Pass deterministic strategy unit tests, leakage checks, cost/slippage sensitivity, walk-forward holdout, risk-limit enforcement, duplicate-order/idempotency tests, and a paper-only integration test. No live order is permitted.
entries.benchmark: DreamFinance momentum strategy benchmark: net-of-cost return, volatility, max drawdown, turnover, exposure, signal stability, and reproducibility; never rank by gross return alone.
entries.buddy_demo: Buddy runs `python -m buddy.trading.demo`, explains each signal and next-bar fill, inspects fees/slippage and drawdown, demonstrates a risk-limit rejection, and saves the reproducible paper-only report. No live broker, credentials, or orders are available.

entries.title: System Design for AI Agents – Building a Multi-Agent PR Reviewer
entries.objective: Design a fault-tolerant multi-agent pull-request reviewer that applies senior-engineer judgment through explicit review dimensions, auditable findings, confidence, and independent verification.
implementation_steps: Map the existing human PR-review process into triggers, inputs, outputs, risk tiers, and approval boundaries.
Define failure modes including hallucinated findings, missed defects, tool timeouts, partial agent results, prompt injection, and unavailable model providers.
Create four specialist review perspectives: security, code quality, tests, and documentation/maintainability.
Implement a fan-out/fan-in orchestration pattern with bounded concurrency, timeouts, retries, cancellation, and partial-result handling.
Define structured finding records with file/line, evidence, severity, confidence, reproducibility, and remediation guidance.
Design durable state and memory schemas for PR identity, commit SHA, findings, reviewer decisions, and prior resolved regressions.
Compare LangGraph state-machine orchestration with Temporal durable workflows; choose based on replay, retries, persistence, and operations needs.
Run each specialist against the exact immutable PR head SHA and collect tool/version provenance.
Require an independent verifier to challenge findings and test the proposed fixes against the original request.
Deduplicate findings, suppress unsupported claims, and distinguish blocking defects from suggestions.
Publish a concise review report with confidence and evidence; request human approval for changes and all merge decisions.
Evaluate on seeded defect suites and historical PRs with precision, recall, false-positive rate, escaped-defect rate, latency, and cost.
entries.practice: Buddy reviews a deliberately seeded test PR using separate security, quality, test, and documentation agents, then has an independent verifier challenge each finding.
entries.assessment: Pass seeded defect detection, false-positive controls, malicious PR-content isolation, timeout/partial-agent recovery, exact-commit anchoring, evidence validation, and human-approval tests. Auto-merge remains disabled.
entries.benchmark: DreamCo PR Guardian benchmark: precision/recall by severity, false-positive rate, verified-fix rate, regression escape rate, review latency, and per-review cost.
entries.buddy_demo: Buddy invokes the DreamCo PR Review Guardian workflow, classifies the diff, maps changed files through config/change-impact-test-policy.json, runs the focused tests and Repository Test Matrix, checks security and dependency risks, summarizes evidence and unresolved risks, and requests human approval. It never auto-merges or approves its own changes.

entries.title: AI Agents For Beginners – OpenClaw Case Study
entries.objective: Teach the foundations of LLM agents, the distinction between workflows and autonomous loops, structured tool use, memory, guardrails, approvals, and sandboxed execution.
implementation_steps: Explain tokens, context windows, model outputs, sampling, and common hallucination/failure modes.
Contrast deterministic workflows with agents that choose the next action based on state and tool results.
Build a minimal agent loop with explicit state, bounded steps, and a stop condition.
Define tool contracts with JSON schemas, input validation, output validation, and permission scopes.
Add specialist agents for orchestration, research, memory, and code/automation with explicit responsibilities.
Persist sessions and memory with provenance, retention, tenant isolation, and deletion controls.
Add structured output validation, input/output guardrails, policy checks, and tool allowlists.
Run risky tools inside isolated sandboxes with resource limits and no ambient host credentials.
Add human approval for external side effects, spending, account changes, publishing, and production deployments.
Build evaluations for tool correctness, task completion, recovery, safety violations, latency, and cost.
Study OpenClaw's architecture as a case study and map transferable patterns to Buddy without importing unreviewed skills.
entries.practice: Buddy builds a local task agent that can read a fixture, call an allowlisted calculator/search mock, retain session memory, and ask approval before a simulated side effect.
entries.assessment: Pass tool-schema validation, prompt-injection resistance, memory isolation, sandbox boundary, step-limit, approval-gate, and reproducibility tests.
entries.benchmark: DreamAgents foundational agent benchmark: task success, tool-call validity, recovery, policy violations, and cost per completed task.
entries.buddy_demo: Demonstrate workflow-vs-agent comparison, four specialist roles, persistent memory, a tool call, sandbox rejection, and approval pause/resume.

entries.title: OpenClaw Full Tutorial for Beginners
entries.objective: Study a local autonomous assistant architecture covering gateway setup, onboarding, skills, memory, messaging connectors, health checks, and sandbox security.
implementation_steps: Understand the gateway as the control plane for sessions, tools, events, and channel connections.
Document prerequisites, installation options, supported model providers, and environment configuration.
Create an isolated local workspace and initialize the assistant through a guided onboarding flow.
Configure model access, local state, session persistence, and remote-access boundaries.
Run health checks and security audits before connecting any external channel.
Inspect workspace and memory files; define safe persistence, provenance, and retention behavior.
Implement skill manifests in YAML/Markdown with explicit tools, scopes, dependencies, and risk levels.
Connect a messaging adapter in a test workspace and validate sender identity, pairing, and permission checks.
Build a small original email skill using a mock inbox and explicit send approval.
Configure multi-agent roles and session switching without sharing private memory across users.
Run tools inside Docker sandbox modes and test filesystem, network, process, and credential restrictions.
Add skill review, version pinning, revocation, audit logs, and rollback for every third-party capability.
entries.practice: Buddy builds a local gateway prototype with one test channel, one original mock email skill, a memory store, and a Docker-isolated tool runner.
entries.assessment: Pass gateway health, channel identity, skill manifest validation, memory isolation, Docker sandbox escape tests, secret redaction, and connector revocation tests.
entries.benchmark: DreamCo OpenClaw-pattern benchmark: setup success, task completion, isolation violations, connector reliability, and recovery.
entries.buddy_demo: Buddy accepts a bounded task, plans it, creates an isolated branch, edits code in a sandbox, runs focused tests, opens a pull request, summarizes evidence, and waits for human approval. It never writes directly to main, exposes secrets, or auto-merges.

entries.title: Build a Self-Healing CI/CD Pipeline with AI
entries.objective: Build a governed self-healing pipeline that diagnoses failed checks, proposes minimal repairs, validates them in isolation, and requires policy-compliant review before integration.
implementation_steps: Collect workflow, job, step, commit, branch, and test-artifact evidence for each failed run.
Classify failures into source defects, test defects, dependency drift, infrastructure outages, permissions, secrets, flaky tests, and external-service failures.
Correlate failures with recent commits and prior incidents without assuming temporal correlation proves causation.
Generate a root-cause hypothesis with exact log evidence and confidence; request more evidence when uncertain.
Create a minimal repair branch from the exact failing commit and restrict writable paths by policy.
Apply a patch proposal in an isolated workspace with no production credentials or unrestricted network access.
Run the smallest relevant test first, then unit, integration, security, contract, and regression suites.
Have an independent reviewer compare the patch with the original task and challenge the test coverage.
Require human approval for protected files, secrets, workflow permissions, production deployment, and merges.
Merge only after required checks and branch protection pass; otherwise preserve the failure and publish a blocked report.
Support rollback, incident linking, and post-repair regression tests.
Track time-to-detect, time-to-diagnose, time-to-repair, false repair rate, recurrence rate, and compute cost.
entries.practice: Buddy receives a synthetic failing GitHub Actions run, identifies its root cause, proposes a one-file patch on a new branch, runs targeted tests, and submits a reviewable PR.
entries.assessment: Pass seeded root-cause cases, least-privilege branch scope, malicious-log prompt injection, secret protection, deterministic tests, independent review, blocked-merge, and rollback tests.
entries.benchmark: DreamCo Self-Healing CI benchmark: diagnosis accuracy, safe repair rate, regression rate, mean time to repair, false repair rate, and spend per incident.
entries.buddy_demo: Buddy runs the repository audit, selects the appropriate quick or standard verification plan, reproduces a failure, proposes a minimal repair on an isolated branch, runs mapped regression tests, checks CI evidence, and opens a reviewable PR. Production certification remains separate from quick checks, and no failed or unverified change is auto-merged.

entries.title: Learn TypeScript - Full Course for Beginners
entries.objective: Build strong TypeScript foundations for safe application code, typed APIs, agent tools, and shared platform contracts.
implementation_steps: Configure a strict TypeScript project and understand compiler options.
Practice primitive, union, literal, array, tuple, enum, and object types.
Model interfaces, type aliases, generics, narrowing, and discriminated unions.
Type functions, async code, errors, and module boundaries.
Validate untrusted runtime input with schemas instead of trusting TypeScript types alone.
Write unit and contract tests and integrate type-checking into CI.
entries.practice: Convert one small DreamCo JavaScript utility into strict TypeScript and expose a validated typed API.
entries.assessment: Pass strict compilation, runtime schema validation, negative type tests, unit tests, and API contract checks.
entries.benchmark: DreamCo TypeScript foundations benchmark: type safety, runtime validation, test coverage, and maintainability.
entries.buddy_demo: Demonstrate type inference, discriminated unions, generic helpers, runtime validation, and CI type-check failure handling.

entries.title: Practical TypeScript – Course for Beginners
entries.objective: Apply TypeScript to realistic modular programs and maintainable application code.
implementation_steps: Set up the compiler and project structure.
Design typed data models and module interfaces.
Implement functions and classes with explicit contracts.
Handle nullable values and unknown external input safely.
Refactor duplicated logic into reusable typed modules.
Test behavior and enforce type checks in CI.
entries.practice: Build a typed division capability registry with validation and tests.
entries.assessment: Pass compile, schema, behavior, regression, and maintainability checks.
entries.buddy_demo: Demonstrate typed registry loading, invalid record rejection, and test-driven refactoring.

entries.title: TypeScript in Express – TypeScript Tutorial
entries.objective: Build typed Express services with validated request boundaries, middleware contracts, and integration tests.
implementation_steps: Initialize an Express TypeScript service with strict compiler settings.
Define typed request, response, and domain contracts.
Implement middleware for authentication, validation, errors, and request IDs.
Validate all external input at runtime.
Separate routes, services, repositories, and adapters.
Add integration tests for success, invalid input, authorization, and failures.
Document OpenAPI contracts and enforce them in CI.
entries.practice: Create a typed Buddy tool API with a read-only endpoint and a permission-gated mock action.
entries.assessment: Pass type checks, runtime validation, auth tests, error contract tests, and OpenAPI parity.
entries.buddy_demo: Demonstrate a typed route, middleware chain, schema rejection, and integration-test output.

entries.title: TypeScript in React – Full Tutorial
entries.objective: Build accessible React interfaces with explicit component props, typed state, reusable hooks, and UI tests.
implementation_steps: Configure React with strict TypeScript.
Type component props, events, children, and reusable components.
Model API data and loading/error states with discriminated unions.
Build typed hooks and context boundaries.
Add accessible interaction patterns and semantic markup.
Test components and user journeys with Testing Library.
Enforce type, lint, accessibility, and test gates in CI.
entries.practice: Build a typed DreamCo division health dashboard component with loading, error, and empty states.
entries.assessment: Pass strict type checking, component tests, keyboard accessibility, and visual-state coverage.
entries.buddy_demo: Demonstrate typed props, safe async state, accessible controls, and UI test failure diagnosis.

routing_rules.objective: Study quantitative strategy research and build a paper-only, risk-controlled implementation.

routing_rules.benchmark: DreamFinance quantitative strategy benchmark.
implementation_steps: Define a testable strategy hypothesis, market universe, benchmark, and time horizon.
Load approved historical or synthetic market data with timestamps and provenance.
Clean and validate prices, calendars, corporate actions, gaps, and duplicate observations.
Prevent look-ahead and survivorship bias by using point-in-time data and time-based splits.
Implement a simple baseline signal before adding more complex factors or machine learning.
Backtest with commissions, spread, slippage, liquidity, and realistic execution assumptions.
Evaluate out-of-sample and walk-forward performance, drawdown, volatility, turnover, and exposure.
Add risk caps, position sizing, loss limits, idempotency, audit logs, and a kill switch.
Run paper trading only and compare expected versus simulated fills.
Require a separate risk and compliance review before any live-trading design is even considered.

routing_rules.objective: Study machine learning foundations and production ML engineering with reproducible data, experiments, evaluation, and deployment.
routing_rules.practice: Build a baseline model, validate data, track experiments, register versions, monitor drift, and deploy only through a tested staging pipeline.
routing_rules.assessment: Pass data-quality, train/serve consistency, holdout, model registry, drift alert, rollback, and regression checks.
routing_rules.benchmark: DreamAIInfra ML lifecycle benchmark.
implementation_steps: Define the prediction or decision problem, intended users, target variable, baseline, and evaluation metric.
Record dataset provenance, collection rights, privacy limits, and permitted uses before ingestion.
Profile data quality, missingness, duplicates, label quality, class balance, and temporal structure.
Split train, validation, and holdout data before fitting preprocessing to prevent leakage.
Build a simple baseline and compare candidate models with reproducible configurations.
Use cross-validation and bounded hyperparameter search without touching the final holdout.
Evaluate task-appropriate metrics, calibration, robustness, subgroup performance, and failure cases.
Log data fingerprints, code commit, parameters, metrics, and artifacts in MLflow or an equivalent tracker.
Register immutable model versions with model cards, provenance, and approval state.
Serve predictions through a validated API with consistent training/serving features.
Monitor input drift, prediction drift, delayed labels, and performance decay.
Release gradually with canary checks, rollback, and a documented retraining trigger.
routing_rules.buddy_demo: Train a small synthetic-data classifier, validate the dataset, log an experiment, register a version, serve it through a local API, and demonstrate drift alerts and rollback.

routing_rules.objective: Study automated CI/CD, root-cause analysis, safe repair proposals, and governed deployment.
routing_rules.practice: Reproduce a seeded failure, collect logs, propose a minimal patch, run targeted tests, and require independent review.
routing_rules.assessment: Pass least-privilege, secret-safety, regression, approval, and rollback tests.
routing_rules.benchmark: DreamCo self-healing CI/CD benchmark.
implementation_steps: Collect exact workflow, job, step, commit, and artifact evidence from a failed run.
Classify the failure as code, test, dependency, infrastructure, permissions, secret, flaky test, or external service.
Generate a root-cause hypothesis with quoted evidence and confidence; do not guess from the workflow name.
Create a repair branch from the exact failing commit and constrain writable paths.
Apply a minimal patch in an isolated workspace without production credentials.
Run focused tests, then the relevant integration, security, contract, and regression suites.
Use an independent reviewer to challenge the diagnosis and verify that tests cover the original failure.
Require human approval for workflow permissions, secrets, protected files, deployment, and merge.
Merge only when branch protection and required checks pass; otherwise preserve a blocked state.
Record repair provenance, rollback instructions, recurrence, time-to-diagnose, time-to-repair, and false-repair rate.
routing_rules.buddy_demo: Inject a synthetic CI failure, have Buddy diagnose it from logs, patch a branch, run regression tests, obtain independent review, and stop before a human-controlled merge.

Track experiments, parameters, metrics, and artifacts in MLflow.
Register model versions and define promotion aliases such as candidate, champion, and rollback.
Use a feature store or shared feature definitions to prevent training-serving skew.
Validate raw and transformed data with explicit schemas and expectations.
Serve the registered model behind FastAPI with authentication and runtime input validation.
Containerize the service and pin dependencies for reproducible environments.
Add CI tests for data contracts, model quality, API behavior, and package security.
Monitor drift and model decay using delayed labels and alert thresholds.
Deploy to staging, canary a release, inspect metrics, and roll back on regressions.
